item.research_question: Can independently controllable multiple coherent precipitation structures be tailored by stepwise thermo-mechanical processes to generate ultrahigh strength and ductile refractory high-entropy alloys?
item.processing_route: Arc melting of pure metals, homogenization at 1200 °C for 5 h, hot-rolling at 1200 °C (80% reduction), cold-rolling at 25 °C (75% reduction), annealing at 900 °C for 5 min, and aging at 650 °C for 20 h followed by water quenching
item.test_conditions: Uniaxial tensile tests at room temperature (strain rate 5 × 10−4 s−1) and elevated temperatures up to 800 °C (strain rate 10−3 s−1)
key_findings: The alloy achieved an ultrahigh ultimate tensile strength of 2.15 GPa with a tensile ductility of 15% at ambient temperature.
The yield strength of the as-cast structure was ~600 MPa, increasing to ~1.4 GPa after Step I (δ-lamella precipitation) and further to 2.0 GPa after Step II (γ″-particle precipitation).
The alloy retained a high yield strength of 1.05 GPa at 800 °C.
The δ-lamellar precipitates have a width of ~40 nm and a length ranging from 0.5 to 1 μm.
The γ″ precipitates are spheroidal with a size of ~10 nm.
Both the δ and γ″ precipitates were identified with the composition (Ni70Fe5)3(Ta20W5).
The lattice misfit between the γ″ precipitates and the matrix was measured to be ~0.013.
The microstructure remained stable after annealing at 800 °C for 50 h (δ phase) and 40 h (γ″ phase).
item.mechanism: The coherent interfaces of the stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations (SCCPs) facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations; dislocations shear the δ-lamellae leading to coherent misalignment rather than crack formation, while the small size and low lattice misfit of γ″ particles prevent crack initiation at the precipitate-matrix interface, collectively enabling high strength and ductility.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study.
item.future_work: The SCCPs design concept may afford a means to develop a wide range of ultrahigh-strength metallic materials by providing a pathway for alloy design.
